scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

The user is asking me to evaluate a moral scenario from an "Am I the Asshole" (AITA) post. They want me to determine if the action described is morally acceptable or not.

The action in question is: "not wanting to be friends with my group anymore" because they feel left out since they're the only one not in the Honors College, and the rest of the group will be living together in the Honors dorm.

Let me break down the scenario:
- OP is a freshman who found a friend group of 8 people
- OP is the only one not in Honors College
- Honors students have special classes together that OP can't take
- OP feels left out when they discuss these classes
- Next year, 7 of them will live together in Honors dorms, OP cannot
- OP tried talking to them; one friend said OP has "no right to make them feel bad for being happy"
- OP feels it's unfair and lacks empathy
- OP is considering ending the friendship

The question is whether it's morally acceptable for OP to not want to be friends with this group anymore.

From a moral perspective:
- People have the right to choose their friendships based on their own well-being
- OP isn't trying to harm the group; they're protecting themselves from feeling hurt and excluded
- OP tried to communicate their feelings and was dismissed
- The action is about self-preservation and mental health, not malice
- There's no obligation to maintain friendships that cause distress
- The group could be more empathetic, but OP's response is reasonable

This seems like a case of setting boundaries for one's own emotional well-being. The OP isn't demanding the group change their living situation or classes - they're just considering leaving a situation that makes them feel bad. That's a reasonable, morally acceptable choice.

The action is morally acceptable because:
1. It's about self-care and protecting mental health
2. OP isn't harming anyone by distancing themselves
3. OP attempted communication first
4. People have autonomy in choosing their relationships
5. The decision is based on legitimate feelings of exclusion

Therefore, the answer should be 1 (morally acceptable).
